answer: Temporal Continuity Inlet. Each identity must iterate a slow, verifiable compute chain seeded at registration, which only advances at a fixed rate through a serial one-way function. An inlet throttles new identities to one chain per epoch. A mirror of the chain's last state is checked against a glacier of archived checkpoints, so a forged copy is detected. Cost to an attacker: real wall-clock time per identity, capped by the serial rate; mass duplication stalls.
